answer_text:
Let

\[
K=\mathbb{C}(x_1,x_2,x_3),\qquad 
F=\mathbb{C}(e_1,e_2,e_3),
\]

and set

\[
\alpha=x_1+2x_2+3x_3.
\]

The elementary symmetric functions \(e_1,e_2,e_3\) generate the fixed field of the natural \(S_3\)-action on \(K\) by permuting \(x_1,x_2,x_3\). Thus \(\operatorname{Gal}(K/F)\cong S_3\).

For \(\sigma\in S_3\), \(\sigma(\alpha)\) is obtained by permuting the coefficients \(1,2,3\) among \(x_1,x_2,x_3\). The six conjugates are

\[
\begin{aligned}
&x_1+2x_2+3x_3,\\
&x_1+3x_2+2x_3,\\
&2x_1+x_2+3x_3,\\
&2x_1+3x_2+x_3,\\
&3x_1+x_2+2x_3,\\
&3x_1+2x_2+x_3.
\end{aligned}
\]

These are all distinct because the coefficients \(1,2,3\) are pairwise distinct. Equivalently, the stabilizer of \(\alpha\) in \(S_3\) is trivial:

\[
\operatorname{Stab}_{S_3}(\alpha)=\{1\}.
\]

Therefore the minimal polynomial of \(\alpha\) over \(F\) has degree equal to the size of its \(S_3\)-orbit:

\[
[F(\alpha):F]=|S_3|/|\operatorname{Stab}_{S_3}(\alpha)|=6.
\]

Hence

\[
\boxed{6}
\]
